lines: Share an agent with your team, and choose who on the team can reach each project’s cards and vault.
Before your AI runs SQL that could delete data, a second model reads it and tells you what it does.
Sharing a card from your team’s project no longer stalls on uploading, so your link is ready in a few clicks.
Linking a big project to a team no longer stalls sync, so every card reaches your team.
Sign in to Weft with GitHub. Your Google account still connects Gmail, Drive and Calendar in Settings.
The phone app now offers Sign in with email, and its TestFlight link reopens once Apple approves it.
Link a repo to your team, so your teammates’ cards show up on your board and your vault is shared securely.
Fold your AI’s question down with the chevron, so you can read the reply above it before you answer.
The copilot is off now, so Weft spends nothing in the background on a copilot you don’t use.
Weft runs on Windows now, on Intel or ARM: install it once and it updates itself, like on the Mac.
Dictate on Windows too: whisper ships inside Weft, so there's nothing else to install.
Take over a teammate's card: ask them to hand it over, or take it now and pick up where they left off.
A linked project's cards sync to your team, so the team's board holds everyone's work, not one person's.
Turn on a folder's Sync and it joins the team too; switch it off and on again and its older cards move over.
Your teammates' cards for a linked project show on your desktop board, read-only, with whose Mac runs each.
Give Weft a project and one button installs the deps, asks for your keys, and shows the app.
Weft is on your phone: each card shows its page, full screen, with your AI's last sentence below.
Share a card and it gets its own address, a preview that unfurls in Slack, and a choice to hide the chat.
Dictate in any app: press ⌥' anywhere on your Mac, and Weft types what you say where you're typing
A Weft Worker's cards now work like your Mac's: their pages in the pane, the live simulator, the browser and the vault
A shared thread gets your own address and a link preview, and can hide the chat to share it as a mini app
Imported GitHub issues can now work themselves: choose where each project lands them, and your AI runs the issue.
Design the agent starts a thread that interviews you, then writes a real agent with its own soul.
Weft now checks its own bundle on launch, so a broken update tells you to reinstall instead of dying.
Your vault now follows you across machines, so your AI finds the same keys on every Mac.
Esc says where it took you, so you know which view you landed in.
Name your models, so every menu shows the model you'll actually run.
The copilot now brings you ideas, not a list of cards, and speaks up at most three times a day.
The Skills menu opens over the whole window now, so nothing gets cut off in a narrow panel.
Puku threads no longer say "Not logged in" in projects that use Puku's API themselves.
Cloning shows its progress, so you know what's happening before your thread starts.
Fold any column to a strip, and let the fullest ones spread out when you need the room.
Press Z to reopen the last card you had open, so you never lose your place.
Your board now reads like a spreadsheet: every card on one sheet, searchable as you type
Sign in to Weft on first launch, so your profile, Project Sync and share links are ready
The New thread dialog picks the model and the agent together, so a thread starts in your voice
Dictate in any app: press ⌥' anywhere on your Mac, and Weft types what you say where you're typing
A Weft Worker's cards now work like your Mac's: their pages in the pane, the live simulator, the browser and the vault
A shared thread gets your own address and a link preview, and can hide the chat to share it as a mini app
